title: Transfer learning grades oral epithelial dysplasia in patient-level held-out histology images
summary: A retrospective study compared learned classifiers for four-grade oral epithelial dysplasia assessment using 3,777 histopathology tissue strips from 94 patients. Images were divided into 15,108 patches after patient-level partitioning. Xception with ReLU achieved reported patch-level test accuracy of 85.19% and weighted F1 of 85.36%; several alternative configurations performed worse or failed to train. The result is limited to this institutional dataset and 128-by-128-pixel patches carrying labels inherited from their parent images. It does not establish whole-slide grading, prospective performance or clinical diagnostic utility.
ai_technology: ImageNet-pretrained CNN transfer learning, including Xception and DenseNet201; ViT comparison
organization: Institute of Advanced Study in Science and Technology; Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research; Arya Wellness Centre; North East Cancer Hospital and Research Institute

evidence.tested: On 3,777 H&E tissue strips from 94 patients, patient-level splits were used; best Xception/ReLU reached 85.19% test accuracy and 85.36% weighted F1 at patch level.
evidence.unknown: Institutional dataset; patch-level evaluation with inherited image labels and possible local label noise; no independently external institution, whole-slide aggregation or prospective clinical validation established.
evidence.ai_role: Transfer-learned image classifiers evaluated four-grade histopathology classification on held-out patients; AI provided the classifier performance and training-convergence findings.

source_review.scope: Publisher abstract, relevant dataset/partitioning, model-training and evaluation Methods, Results and limitation sections independently read in full publisher HTML; no independent reanalysis.
